q: In 1905, Albert Einstein proposed that light must also be thought of as particle or ____.
e: Einstein's photoelectric effect theory established that light energy is quantized into discrete packets called photons.

q: In 1923, Louis de Broglie proposed that the wavelength of a material particle would be related to its ____.
e: De Broglie hypothesized that all matter exhibits wave-particle duality, with wavelength inversely proportional to momentum.

q: The existence of matter waves were first experimentally confirmed by Thomson's cathode ray diffraction experiment and the ____ experiment for electrons.
e: The Davisson-Germer experiment demonstrated electron diffraction, proving the wave nature of matter.

q: In ____ microscope, the wave nature of electrons is used instead of light.
e: Electron microscopes use the extremely short de Broglie wavelength of electrons to achieve high-resolution imaging.

q: An integral number of de Broglie wavelengths associated with a revolving electron must fit in the ____ of an orbit.
e: This condition creates standing waves, explaining why only certain discrete electron orbits are stable.
